The fixed-destination allow-list already permits the sender's own DM as a target for replies, but reminders never use it.
scenario: Chloe DMs 'remind me to take my antibiotics at 9pm'. At 21:00 the house group sees '⏰ take my antibiotics', which is a private health detail posted to everyone and addressed to no one.
repro: audit-repro/actions/reminders.test.ts, 'a PERSONAL reminder set privately in a DM is broadcast…': row.deliverChatId===HOUSE and the delivered body is '⏰ take my antibiotics'. PASS.
fixDirection: For member_dm-origin reminders (or first-person ones), deliver to the authenticated sender's DM (origin.chatId), a code-resolved allow-listed target, or at least confirm the destination.

title: Recurring reminders ('every friday') silently become one-offs, and only one reminder per message is possible
mechanism: The extraction schema is a single {isReminder, whenText, content}, with no recurrence field and no array. parseWhen('every friday at 8pm') resolves to the next Friday. After delivery the row is marked 'sent' and nothing reschedules it. A message holding two reminders keeps only one. The spec requires recurrence for dated events.
scenario: Chloe: 'remind us every friday at 8pm to put the bins out'. Baumy reacts 👍, fires once this Friday, and never again, while the house believes it's a standing reminder. 'Remind me at 5 to defrost the chicken and at 7 to put it in the oven' produces only one ⏰.
repro: audit-repro/actions/reminders.test.ts, 'every friday at 8pm silently becomes ONE Friday': one row, status 'sent' after delivery, no new row, and the schema keys are exactly [isReminder, whenText, content]. PASS. The multi-reminder case is proven by the schema shape (code-read).
fixDirection: Extend the extraction to a list of reminders with an optional recurrence rule, reschedule on markSent, and at minimum tell the user when recurrence was requested but not supported.

title: A soft forget hides the fact but the source message stays active, so Baumy keeps answering with the 'forgotten' info
mechanism: Soft mode only sets is_current=false on facts. Notes are scrubbed only on purge. The soft card says "I'll forget (hidden, reversible)", but the verbatim evidence note (e.g. 'Zosia is staying in my room this weekend') stays is_active and embedded. The hybrid retrieval in the reply path returns it, so the next question is answered from it. The memory repro shows the soft-forgotten fact also resurfaces as a lineage parent.
scenario: Chloe: 'forget that Zosia is staying in my room', then taps ✅ and sees 'Forgotten — 1 fact'. Later Marco asks 'where's Zosia sleeping?' and Baumy answers 'in Chloe's room, per Chloe'.
repro: audit-repro/actions/forget.test.ts, 'SOFT forget hides the fact but the source note stays active…': forgetMemory soft gives facts=1, then retrieve('where is Zosia staying this weekend') still returns the note. PASS.
fixDirection: Make soft forget also deactivate the matched notes (reversibly, e.g. is_active=false) or exclude them from retrieval, so 'hidden' means hidden from replies.

title: Forget resolution misses facts about a named subject: values match only object_value, and subject lookup needs every attribute word to appear literally
mechanism: A named value ('Zosia') is matched with facts.object_value ~* only, never the subject entity, so facts whose subject is Zosia are not proposed. The subject path runs only when attribute is non-empty, and it requires every attribute word longer than 2 characters to appear in 'predicate value' as a substring, so natural phrasing ('where she is sleeping' against staying_in) finds nothing. Result: soft mode replies "That's only in past messages…" or "Nothing like that in my memory" even though a current fact exists.
scenario: Chloe: 'forget everything about Zosia'. Baumy replies "That's only in past messages, not a fact I can just hide", but the fact zosia→staying_in→chloe's room is current and keeps grounding answers.
repro: audit-repro/actions/forget.test.ts: findMemoryToForget({values:['Zosia'],subject:'Zosia',attribute:''}) returns facts=[] with noteIds=1. {subject:'Zosia',attribute:'where she is sleeping'} returns facts=[]. Both PASS.
fixDirection: When a subject resolves to an entity (or a value equals an entity name), propose that entity's current facts, and match attributes loosely (any word or predicate synonyms) since the human confirm-tap is the precision gate.

title: Un-directed group text creates reminders, where spec transcript (b) and the master spec require a directed request
mechanism: decide() returns 'reminder' for any house message classified intent=reminder with confidence >=0.7. There is no directedness check. Spec acceptance transcript (b) says the un-directed 'someone remind everyone to clear the front room Friday night' must produce no reminder row, and T8 says 'reminders only from explicit directed creation'. (AGENTS.md makes reminders auto-commit, but it does not remove the directed requirement.)
scenario: Theo tells Jules 'remind me to text you about the van tomorrow' in the group. Baumy posts '⏰ text you about the van' to the whole house tomorrow.
repro: audit-repro/spec-gap/chat-routing.test.ts 'spec product.md transcript (b)' asserts a baumy_reminders row is created from an un-directed Theo message. PASS.
fixDirection: Require `directed` (or the DM lane) for reminder creation, as the spec's write-gate keyed on origin × directedness does.

title: A shopping-list op returns early, so any question or request in the same message is never answered, even when directed
mechanism: When the list step handles the message it returns { decision: 'list' } before the reminder and reply blocks. In the group an add/check-off only gets a reaction, even when directed (@mention / console topic) and even when the verdict is intent=question/respond=answer.
scenario: Chloe: '@baumy add milk to the list — and what's the wifi password?' Milk is added and Baumy reacts 🧠, but the question gets no answer.
repro: audit-repro/actions/list.test.ts, 'list early-return swallows…': decision 'list', REPLY_SYSTEM never called, no send, reaction 🧠. PASS.
fixDirection: After a handled list op, still run the reply path when the message is directed or contains a question beyond the list op (or skip the list short-circuit when intent=question and op≠query).

title: List ops are also captured as memory notes and never retired, so later questions ground on stale 'we're out of milk'
mechanism: Capture runs before, and independently of, the list step. 'we're out of milk' or 'buy milk' becomes an active evidence note (and possibly a fact), and nothing deactivates it when the item is checked off. A later question that doesn't go through the list extractor ('do we have milk?') is answered from memory, not the list.
scenario: Monday: 'we're out of milk'. Tuesday: 'got the milk' (checked off). Wednesday: '@baumy do we have milk?' Baumy: 'Chloe said we're out of milk'.
repro: audit-repro/actions/list.test.ts, 'list ops are ALSO captured…': after add plus check-off, memory_items still has an active "we're out of milk". PASS (the stale answer itself depends on the model, so it is inferred).
fixDirection: Skip capture for messages fully handled as list ops (or capture at low salience and deactivate on check-off), and route list-state questions to the list table.

title: /bug, /weekly, /guests, /reminders and /recent run in any chat a member types them in (before the lane check), posting house memory into foreign groups
mechanism: The report and house-report branches check only roster.isMember(fromId). They run before `if (origin.lane === 'ignore') return`, and reply via sayHouse(chatId) to the inbound chat. A housemate typing /guests in another group the bot belongs to gets the house's guest/room report posted there.
scenario: Marco adds Baumy to his football group and types /guests. Baumy posts who is sleeping in which room at the house to that group.
repro: Not written: straightforward from the branch order at ingest.ts:106-155 vs 218.
fixDirection: Require origin.lane ∈ {house, member_dm} for report commands, like every other reply path.
